blocks.value: UI UX Design combines user interface and user experience design, together facilitating the designing of digital products like web pages, mobile apps, video games and software applications.

UI Design majorly focuses on the overall look and feel of the user interfaces to encourage customers like you to stick with the brand or product for a long time while UX Design is all about the overall user experience and functionality of the digital product.

UI/UX Syllabus build to provide the students with practical projects, teach them some of the most important industry tools, and prepare them for interviews, focusing on creating intuitive and engaging digital experiences. The course helps the UI/UX Graduates to design user-friendly digital products and blend creativity with tech.

After pursuing UI/UX Courses , the graduates can find jobs in roles like UX Designer, UI Designer, Researcher, Information Architect, or Product Designer, offering good growth from junior to senior or even leadership positions.

faqs.question: Why pursue UI and UX Design courses?
faqs.answer: Some of the pointers to know why you should pursue UI/UX Design courses are mentioned below for your reference - UI/UX design needs proficiency in multiple areas such as cognitive psychology, visual design, and usability research. Designers must combine technical knowledge with an understanding of human behavior. A well-designed user interface and experience can increase user engagement rates along with their retention rates . For example, studies show that the users leave the products that are difficult to use and understand. UI/UX design provides many job options such as in house positions, agency roles, and freelance opportunities. Hope this helps!!!

faqs.question: Do all UI/UX designers need to know coding?
faqs.answer: Coding can be a great skill for all designers. It is not a strict or mandatory requirement. Many UI UX roles also involve creating wireframes, prototypes, and visual designs using tools like Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD. In these, programming knowledge is not exactly required. But having knowledge of coding can be very much useful when working with the developers. Know more about - UI UX Design courses

faqs.question: What is the general admission process for UI/UX Design courses?
faqs.answer: You need to first begin by checking the eligibility criteria for UI UX Design courses as set by multiple colleges. Then you have t take the relevant entrance exams and get excellent marks and a high rank in order to get a seat at top design colleges. After the exam results are out and you have got your marks, you then have to appear for studio tests or submit a strong portfolio to show your skills. After that you will have to take part in the counseling rounds that are meant for seat allotment based on your performance in the written test and other admission rounds. faqs.question: What does a UI/UX Designer do?
faqs.answer: UI UX Designers have many responsibilities to fulfill that are listed below for your reference - Plan and implement new designs. Interpret data and qualitative feedback. Optimize existing user interface designs. Test for experience Plan and conduct user research and competitor analysis. Create user stories, personas, and storyboards. Determine information architecture and create sitemaps. Create prototypes and wireframes. Communicate scenarios to hypothetical users, interaction models, and screen designs to other people working on a product. Work as a team with creative heads and designers to incorporate brand identity into the given product. Develop app mockups and specs. Perform competitive analysis of other websites operating in the same space. Prepare a customer analysis report based on demographics, targets, and transactions. Coordinate with the design, product, sales, and marketing teams for creating and marketing an effective final product.

UI/UX Syllabus: Core Topics and Structure

In UI/UX design courses from the best MOOCs , the syllabi will cover the fundamentals of the design principles, conducting user research through interviews, and mastering tools like Adobe and/or Figma. The structure may differ depending on the learner’s expertise level.
Here is a synthesised version of a comprehensive UI/UX design course syllabus that is covered within a few months.

value: What is UI/UX Design, Importance of User-Centric Design, Design Thinking Process, Core Principles, Role of UX in Product Development Lifecycle
Understanding User Needs, User Research Methods, User Personas, User Journey Maps, Data Analysis
Organising Information, Card Sorting, Tree Testing, Sitemaps, Wireframes
User Flows, Microinteractions, Designing for Different Devices, Prototyping Tools
Colour Theory, Typography, Layout, Visual Hierarchy, Design Systems, UI Design Patterns
Advanced User Research Methods, Data Analysis, A/B Testing, Eye-Tracking Studies
Inclusive Design, WCAG Guidelines, Accessibility Testing Tools

blocks.value: Usually at the end of most UI/UX courses, you will have to participate in specialisation-based capstone projects. Some courses also come with quizzes or peer reviewed projects after each chapter that solidify your learning for real world scenarios.
UI/UX Design Course Syllabus for Beginners
Beginner level UI/UX courses have several topic categories, where the syllabus differ for each. Some beginner level courses will still require knowledge of UI/UX in general.
For example, if you are planning to learn Figma tool, you may want to focus just on this. Still, you will need to have a familiarity to what constitutes prototyping.

More so, the curriculum for a Figma certification course will not be as beginner-friendly as a course on introduction to UI/UX design. This is because, in the latter, you will have to learn what design principles are, how they correlate with product development, and so on. In the former, you will learn to use the tool based on the principles that constitute UI/UX design - and the instructor will already assume you have a grasp on the topics.

The courses for those already in the UI/UX field are more specialised in terms of the discipline’s subcategories. One can specialise in UI/UX writing, UI/UX research, prototyping, etc. You may want to look into the UI/UX salary in India to choose the specialisation you are interested in.
